newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WESTERN PROVINCE THRASH SWD 107-23.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WESTERN PROVINCE THRASH SWD 107-23.

text.p: Western Province competely outclassed Currie Cup minnows South Western Districts 107-23 (halftime 36-16) in their match at Mossel Bay on Saturday.
After being beaten 113-11 by Free State in Bloemfontein last weekend, the writing was one the wall for the home side, as they trailed 36-16 at the break.

For the second successive week they conceded 17 tries, and had flyhalf Louis Koen not missed a few easy conversions last week's record Currie Cup score might have been eclisped. Koen converted 11 of the tries to add to his two tries.

SWD coach Piet de Jager made several appearances on the field during breaks in play, as he attempted to pass on tips to his players, but with the exception of hard working flank Jacques Wolfaardt, eighthman Theo Kuyler, centre Hugo Beukes and wing Pau Treu, the home team's players looked out of their class playing in the country's premier rugby competition.
South Western Districts: Try: John van Standen, Herman Freiboth. Conversion: Jurie Coetzee (2). Penalties: Coetzee (3).

Western Province: Tries: Nico Wegner (2), Joggie Viljoen (3), Louis Koen (2), Breyton Paulse (3), Pieter Roussouw (2), Garry Pagel (1), Robbie Brink (2), Fritz van Heerden, Justin Swart. Conversions: Koen (11).
